Official Source: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India
Authority: Ministry of MSME, MoSD&E, and Department of Financial Services
Portal URL: https://pmvishwakarma.gov.in/
Source ID: src-001
chunks.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme Guidelines
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India

chunks.chunk_text:
PM Vishwakarma is a Central Sector Scheme launched to provide end-to-end support to artisans and craftspeople who work with their hands and tools. The scheme aims to:
- Enable the recognition of artisans and craftspeople as Vishwakarmas, making them eligible to avail all the benefits under the Scheme.
- Help them upgrade their skills and provide them with relevant and suitable training opportunities.
- Support them with better and modern tools to enhance their capability, productivity, and quality of products.
- Provide them with access to collateral-free credit and reduce the cost of credit by providing interest subvention.
- Provide them with incentives for digital transactions to encourage digital empowerment.
- Provide them with a platform for brand promotion and market linkages.
chunks.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme Guidelines
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India

chunks.chunk_text:
The scheme covers artisans and craftspeople engaged in 18 traditional family-based trades:
1. Carpenter (Suthar)
2. Boat Maker
3. Armourer
4. Blacksmith (Lohar)
5. Hammer and Tool Kit Maker
6. Locksmith
7. Sculptor (Moortikar, stone carver), Stone breaker
8. Goldsmith (Sonar)
9. Potter (Kumhaar)
10. Cobbler (Charmakar) / Shoesmith / Footwear artisan 11. Masons (Raajmistri)
12. Basket / Mat / Broom Maker / Coir Weaver 13. Doll & Toy Maker (Traditional)
14. Barber (Naai) 15. Garland maker (Malakaar)
16. Washerman (Dhobi) 17. Tailor (Darzi)
18. Fishing Net Maker
chunks.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme Guidelines
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India

chunks.chunk_text:
- An artisan or craftsperson working with hands and tools and engaged in one of the 18 family-based traditional trades mentioned above in the unorganised sector on self-employment basis.
- The minimum age of the beneficiary should be 18 years on the date of registration.
- The beneficiary should be actively engaged in the concerned trade on the date of registration and should not have availed credit-based schemes of the Central Government or State Government for self-employment or business development (e.g. PMEGP, PM SVANidhi, Mudra) in the past 5 years.
- The registration and benefits under the Scheme shall be restricted to one member of the family. For the purpose of the Scheme, a 'family' is defined as consisting of the husband, wife, and unmarried children.
- A person in government service and their family members shall not be eligible under the Scheme.
chunks.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme Guidelines
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India

chunks.chunk_text: The scheme provides five major types of benefits to registered Vishwakarmas:
chunks.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme Guidelines
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India

chunks.chunk_text: - Recognition through PM Vishwakarma Certificate and ID Card acknowledging their traditional skills.
chunks.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme Guidelines
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India

chunks.chunk_text:
- Basic Training of 5 to 7 days (40 hours) with a daily training stipend of Rs 500 per day.
- Advanced Training of 15 days (120 hours) or more for interested candidates, with training stipend of Rs 500 per day.
chunks.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme Guidelines
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India

chunks.chunk_text: - A toolkit incentive grant of up to Rs 15,000 provided in the form of e-vouchers / digital voucher upon commencement of Basic Training.
chunks.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme Guidelines
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India

chunks.chunk_text:
- Collateral-free Enterprise Development Loans:
- First Tranche: Up to Rs 1,00,000 (repayable over 18 months).
- Second Tranche: Up to Rs 2,00,000 (repayable over 30 months) for beneficiaries who have availed the first tranche, maintained a standard repayment record, adopted digital transactions, or completed advanced skill training.
- Concessional Interest Rate: A concessional interest rate of 5% is charged from the beneficiary, with an interest subvention cap of 8% paid by the Government of India.
- Credit Guarantee fees are fully borne by the Government of India.
chunks.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme Guidelines
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India

chunks.chunk_text: - An incentive of Re 1 per digital transaction for a maximum of up to 100 transactions per month is credited to the beneficiary's bank account.
chunks.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme Guidelines
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India

chunks.chunk_text: - Marketing assistance in the form of quality certification, branding, onboarding on e-commerce platforms such as GeM, advertising, and trade fairs.
chunks.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme Guidelines
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India

chunks.chunk_text:
Registration is conducted through Common Service Centres (CSCs) via biometric authentication on the PM Vishwakarma Portal.
Required verification documents:
- Aadhaar Card (mandatory identity proof).
- Mobile number linked to Aadhaar.
- Active Bank Account details (Bank Account number, IFSC code).
- Ration Card / Family Declaration.
Verification is conducted through a three-stage process:
1. Stage 1: Gram Panchayat / Urban Local Body (ULB) verification.
2. Stage 2: District Implementation Committee (DIC) screening.
3. Stage 3: National Steering Committee approval.
chunks.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme Guidelines
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India

chunks.section: e-Shram Portal Guidelines and Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.title: e-Shram Portal Guidelines and Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India

chunks.chunk_text: The Ministry of Labour & Employment has developed the e-Shram portal for creating a centralized National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW). The database is seeded with Aadhaar and aims to deliver social security benefits and welfare schemes implemented by the Central and State Governments to informal workers.
chunks.title: e-Shram Portal Guidelines and Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India

chunks.chunk_text: An unorganised worker is any worker who is a home-based worker, self-employed worker, or a wage worker working in the unorganised sector. An unorganised sector enterprise includes any establishment or business owned by individuals or self-employed workers engaged in the production or sale of goods or services, where the enterprise employs fewer than 10 workers.
chunks.title: e-Shram Portal Guidelines and Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India

chunks.chunk_text:
To register on e-Shram, an applicant must satisfy the following conditions:
- Age: The worker must be between 16 and 59 years of age (16 years or above on the date of registration).
- Occupation: Must be engaged in an unorganised sector occupation (e.g. agricultural labour, construction work, domestic work, street vending, transport driving, delivery gig work, tailoring, carpentry, craftsmanship).
- Social Security Exclusion: The worker must NOT be a member of the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) or Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC).
- Tax Exclusion: The worker should NOT be an income tax payee.
- Income Criteria: There is no minimum or maximum income criterion for registering on e-Shram as an unorganised worker, provided the individual is not an income tax payee.
chunks.title: e-Shram Portal Guidelines and Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India

chunks.chunk_text:
Registration on e-Shram is free of charge:
- Mandatory Documents:
1. Aadhaar Number (UIDAI).
2. Mobile Number linked with Aadhaar (for OTP authentication).
3. Active Savings Bank Account details (Account Number, Bank Name, IFSC code).
- Workers who do not have an Aadhaar-linked mobile number can visit the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) or State Seva Kendra for assisted registration using biometric (fingerprint or iris) authentication.
chunks.title: e-Shram Portal Guidelines and Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India

chunks.chunk_text:
Upon successful registration on the e-Shram portal:
- Workers are issued an e-Shram Card featuring a unique 12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN) that is valid across all States and Union Territories of India.
- Clarification on Financial Benefits: Currently, registration on the e-Shram portal serves as a unified registration and identity mechanism for unorganised workers. Registration itself does not disburse direct recurring cash grants or automatic cash allowances unless linked to specific disaster relief or targeted State welfare programs.
- The UAN card enables portable delivery of social security benefits, accidental insurance coverage notifications, and skill development opportunities under Central and State Government schemes.
chunks.title: e-Shram Portal Guidelines and Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India

chunks.section: Chief Minister's Kaushalya Karnataka Yojane (CMKKY) Scheme Guidelines
chunks.title: Chief Minister's Kaushalya Karnataka Yojane (CMKKY) Scheme Framework
chunks.issuing_authority: Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood Department, Government of Karnataka

chunks.chunk_text: Chief Minister's Kaushalya Karnataka Yojane (CMKKY) is the flagship vocational skilling initiative implemented by the Government of Karnataka through the Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood. The primary objective is to enhance the employability and livelihood opportunities of youth across the state through demand-driven market-aligned technical training.
chunks.title: Chief Minister's Kaushalya Karnataka Yojane (CMKKY) Scheme Framework
chunks.issuing_authority: Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood Department, Government of Karnataka

chunks.chunk_text:
- Short-Term Vocational Training: Training courses offered under CMKKY are aligned to the National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF) standards.
- Placement Commitment: Training providers empanelled under the scheme are obligated to ensure wage employment or self-employment placement for at least 70% of certified trainees.
- Industry Partnerships: Training curricula and job roles are formulated in consultation with industry sector skill councils and local employer associations in Karnataka.
- Standardized Certification: Trainees who successfully complete assessments are awarded government-recognized skill certifications.
chunks.title: Chief Minister's Kaushalya Karnataka Yojane (CMKKY) Scheme Framework
chunks.issuing_authority: Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood Department, Government of Karnataka

chunks.chunk_text:
- Target Group: Youth and informal job seekers residing in Karnataka seeking entry-level technical skills or wage employment in organized industries.
- Portal Registration: Aspiring candidates must register online on the Kaushalkar portal (www.kaushalkar.karnataka.gov.in) to select their preferred district, sector, and training centre.
- Documentation: Aadhaar identity proof and educational qualification certificates relevant to the chosen NSQF course level.
- Note on Age & Educational Limits: Course-specific eligibility criteria (such as minimum age and schooling requirement) depend upon the individual Qualification Pack (QP) prescribed by the respective Sector Skill Council.
chunks.title: Chief Minister's Kaushalya Karnataka Yojane (CMKKY) Scheme Framework
chunks.issuing_authority: Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood Department, Government of Karnataka

chunks.section: Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board (KBOCWWB) Overview
chunks.title: Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board Overview
chunks.issuing_authority: Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (KBOCWWB)

chunks.chunk_text: The Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board (KBOCWWB) was established in 2007 under the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996 and the Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Rules, 2006. The Board is responsible for administering the statutory welfare fund raised via construction cess and disbursing social welfare assistance to registered construction workers across Karnataka.
chunks.title: Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board Overview
chunks.issuing_authority: Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (KBOCWWB)

chunks.chunk_text:
- Eligible Trade: Any building or other construction worker engaged in building construction, masonry, carpentry, bar bending, plumbing, electrical installation, painting, demolition, or earthwork within Karnataka.
- Minimum Employment: The worker must have worked for not less than 90 days as a construction worker during the preceding 12 months.
- Age: The applicant must have completed 18 years of age and not reached 60 years of age.
- Required Application Documents: Form V application, Aadhaar card, employer certification / 90-day work certificate (certified by registered contractor, trade union, or labour officer), and active bank account passbook.
chunks.title: Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board Overview
chunks.issuing_authority: Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (KBOCWWB)

chunks.chunk_text:
Registered construction workers holding a valid Board identity card are eligible for various welfare assistance schemes:
- Educational Assistance: Annual scholarships for children of registered construction workers studying in primary, secondary, pre-university, undergraduate, and technical/diploma institutions.
- Toolkits and Equipment: Distribution of safety kits and trade-specific toolkit assistance to enhance on-site safety and technical productivity.
- Marriage Assistance: Financial grant disbursed for the marriage of registered construction workers or their children.
- Maternity Benefit: Financial assistance provided to registered female construction workers during pregnancy and childbirth.
- Accident Relief and Funeral Expenses: Immediate financial relief in the event of accidental death or permanent disablement occurring during construction employment.
- Official Helpline: Labour helpline 155214 is operational for registered worker queries and application status tracking. Note: Exact cash assistance figures are subject to state gazette notifications and require official source verification before disbursement citations.
chunks.title: Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board Overview
chunks.issuing_authority: Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (KBOCWWB)

chunks.section: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0 Overview
chunks.title: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0 Overview
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) / PIB

chunks.chunk_text: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0 was announced under the Skill India Mission to build an agile, future-ready workforce aligned with emerging economic and technological requirements. The scheme prioritizes on-demand training, localized skilling, and industry partnerships across states including Karnataka.
chunks.title: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0 Overview
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) / PIB

chunks.chunk_text:
A core pivot in PMKVY 4.0 is the incorporation of future-oriented skill training tailored to Industry 4.0 demands:
- Emerging Domains: Specialized courses in Artificial Intelligence (AI), Robotics, Internet of Things (IoT), Mechatronics, 3D Printing, Drone Technology, and Green Energy / Electric Vehicles.
- Upskilling Traditional Sectors: Modernizing existing manufacturing, logistics, apparel, and construction vocations through digital and automated tool handling.
chunks.section: 2. Focus on Industry 4.0 and New-Age Roles
chunks.title: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0 Overview
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) / PIB

chunks.chunk_text:
The scheme operates through three primary implementation tracks:
- Short Term Training (STT): Targeted at school/college dropouts and unemployed youth to impart modular vocational skills aligned to NSQF standards.
- Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL): Formally assessing and certifying existing competencies and informal experience of unorganised workers without requiring full-time classroom schooling.
- Special Projects: Custom skilling initiatives designed for marginalized communities, remote districts, and specialized industrial clusters.
- Skill Hubs: Establishing training nodes within existing educational infrastructure (ITIs, Navodaya Vidyalayas, Polytechnics, and Colleges).
chunks.title: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0 Overview
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) / PIB

chunks.chunk_text:
- Training Costs: Training and assessment costs are fully sponsored by the Central Government, offering fee-free participation for eligible candidates.
- Assessment and Digital Credentials: Certification is issued upon independent third-party assessment and recorded as digital verifiable credentials via the Skill India Digital platform.
- Operational Reform: PMKVY 4.0 delinks financial payout milestones to training partners from mandatory placement outcomes, prioritizing holistic candidate competence, foundational digital literacy, and lifelong learning adaptability.
chunks.section: 4. Policy Revisions and Delinking of Placement Rewards
chunks.title: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0 Overview
chunks.issuing_authority: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) / PIB

chunks.section: Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) — Electrician Trade Syllabus & Qualification
chunks.title: CTS Electrician Trade Syllabus and Course Qualification
chunks.issuing_authority: Electronic Sector Skills Council of India (ESSCI) / DGT MSDE

chunks.chunk_text:
The Electrician trade under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) is a nationally recognized vocational course categorized under the Electrical & Electronics sector.
- NSQF Level: Level 4
- Duration: 2 Years (1200 hours per year; 2400 hours total encompassing trade theory, trade practical, workshop calculation & science, engineering drawing, and employability skills).
- Entry Qualification: Passed 10th class examination with Science and Mathematics or its equivalent from a recognized board.
- Minimum Age: 14 years (no upper age limit for CTS admissions).
chunks.title: CTS Electrician Trade Syllabus and Course Qualification
chunks.issuing_authority: Electronic Sector Skills Council of India (ESSCI) / DGT MSDE

chunks.chunk_text:
A certified CTS Electrician acquires foundational and advanced technical competencies:
- Safety Practices: Adherence to Indian Electricity (IE) rules, electrical safety procedures, personal protective equipment (PPE), fire safety, and electric shock first aid.
- Wiring Systems: Planning, executing, and testing domestic, commercial, and industrial electrical wiring in compliance with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) specifications.
- Power Equipment: Installation, operation, routine maintenance, and fault diagnosis of Single Phase and Three Phase AC motors, DC machines, alternators, transformers, and switchgear.
- Measuring Instruments: Practical handling and calibration of multimeters, clamp meters, earth megohmmeters (Megger), oscilloscopes, and energy meters.
- Control Panels: Assembly, wiring, and testing of electrical control panels, starters (DOL, Star-Delta), relays, contactors, and circuit breakers (MCB, MCCB, ELCB/RCCB).
- Renewable Energy Integration: Basic configuration, testing, and maintenance of solar photovoltaic (PV) home lighting systems and uninterrupted power supply (UPS) systems.
chunks.title: CTS Electrician Trade Syllabus and Course Qualification
chunks.issuing_authority: Electronic Sector Skills Council of India (ESSCI) / DGT MSDE

chunks.chunk_text: Graduates are awarded the National Trade Certificate (NTC) issued by NCVT/DGT upon passing the All India Trade Test (AITT). The qualification qualifies individuals for technician roles in state electricity supply companies (ESCOMs), manufacturing plants, railway maintenance depots, construction sites, and independent electrical contracting businesses.
chunks.title: CTS Electrician Trade Syllabus and Course Qualification
chunks.issuing_authority: Electronic Sector Skills Council of India (ESSCI) / DGT MSDE

chunks.section: Qualification Pack — Self Employed Tailor (AMH/Q1947, v2.0)
chunks.title: Qualification Pack — Self Employed Tailor (AMH/Q1947, v2.0)
chunks.issuing_authority: Apparel, Made-ups & Home Furnishing Sector Skill Council (AMHSSC)

chunks.chunk_text:
A Self Employed Tailor operates independently to design, cut, stitch, finish, and repair bespoke garments based on customer specifications and body measurements.
- QP Code: AMH/Q1947, Version 2.0
- NCO Code: NCO-2015/7531.0100 (Tailors and Dressmakers)
- NSQF Level: Level 4
- Minimum Entry Age: 18 Years
- Minimum Educational Qualification: 8th Class pass with 6 months of relevant apparel sector experience, OR 10th Class pass with no prior experience required.
- Training Duration: Typically 300 to 350 hours covering classroom theory, garment lab practicals, entrepreneurship, and soft skills.
chunks.section: 1. Qualification Brief and Job Role Overview
chunks.title: Qualification Pack — Self Employed Tailor (AMH/Q1947, v2.0)
chunks.issuing_authority: Apparel, Made-ups & Home Furnishing Sector Skill Council (AMHSSC)

chunks.chunk_text:
The qualification mandates mastery over five core competencies:
1. Client Consultation and Measurement (AMH/N1947): Taking accurate body measurements, documenting customer preferences, suggesting fabric types, estimating yardage, calculating cost quotes, and scheduling delivery dates.
2. Pattern Drafting and Fabric Cutting (AMH/N1948): Drafting paper patterns for basic and contemporary garments (blouses, kurtas, shirts, trousers, dresses), placing patterns efficiently on fabric to minimize wastage, and cutting panels with industrial cutting shears.
3. Sewing and Assembly Operations (AMH/N1949): Operating manual, motorized, and single-needle lockstitch industrial sewing machines; assembling collars, sleeves, cuffs, pockets, plackets, waistbands, and zippers.
4. Garment Finishing and Quality Inspection (AMH/N1950): Trimming loose threads, pressing and ironing garments, attaching fasteners (hooks, buttons, snaps), checking seam allowances, and conducting final fit inspections.
5. Workshop Safety and Machine Maintenance: Routine cleaning, needle replacement, oiling, bobbin tension adjustment, and adherence to electrical and ergonomic workplace safety standards.
chunks.title: Qualification Pack — Self Employed Tailor (AMH/Q1947, v2.0)
chunks.issuing_authority: Apparel, Made-ups & Home Furnishing Sector Skill Council (AMHSSC)

chunks.chunk_text: Graduates possess the technical and business skills necessary to establish proprietary tailoring micro-enterprises, join boutique design studios, or work as sample tailors in export garment manufacturing factories in Karnataka apparel clusters (e.g. Peenya, Bommanahalli, Doddaballapura).
chunks.title: Qualification Pack — Self Employed Tailor (AMH/Q1947, v2.0)
chunks.issuing_authority: Apparel, Made-ups & Home Furnishing Sector Skill Council (AMHSSC)

chunks.section: Qualification File — Armed Security Guard (NCVET Code 2022/OAFM/MEPSC/05426)
chunks.title: Qualification File — Armed Security Guard (NCVET Code 2022/OAFM/MEPSC/05426)
chunks.issuing_authority: Management & Entrepreneurship and Professional Skills Council (MEPSC)

chunks.chunk_text:
An Armed Security Guard is responsible for providing armed protection to designated personnel, high-value assets, cash-in-transit (CIT) vans, bank premises, and sensitive commercial establishments under the Private Security Agencies (Regulation) Act (PSARA), 2005.
- NCVET File Code: 2022/OAFM/MEPSC/05426
- NCO Code: NCO-2015/5414.0151
- NSQF Level: Level 4
- Minimum Entry Age: 21 Years
- Minimum Educational & Experience Qualifications:
- Class 10th pass from a recognized board, AND
- Minimum 2 years of prior experience in the Armed Forces, Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF), State Police, or recognized paramilitary agencies, OR 3 years of verified private security guard experience with a valid arms license.
- Total Training Duration: 450 Hours (174 Hours Theory + 276 Hours Practical/Range Training; offline classroom and firing range mode).
chunks.section: 1. Job Role Description and Qualification Parameters
chunks.title: Qualification File — Armed Security Guard (NCVET Code 2022/OAFM/MEPSC/05426)
chunks.issuing_authority: Management & Entrepreneurship and Professional Skills Council (MEPSC)

chunks.chunk_text:
The qualification covers stringent legal, physical, and weapon safety competencies:
- Firearms Handling and Maintenance: Safe loading, unloading, clearing, dry firing, cleaning, and maintenance of 12-bore DBBL/SBBL shotguns and permissible handguns; adherence to the Arms Act 1959.
- Range Drill and Target Engagement: Target acquisition, safe drawing, breath control, trigger pull, live ammunition firing drill, and misfire drill under certified range supervisors.
- Access Control and Perimeter Defense: Screening visitors, inspecting vehicles with under-chassis mirrors, operating handheld metal detectors (HHMD) and door frame metal detectors (DFMD), maintaining visitor logs.
- Emergency Response and Crisis Management: Responding to armed robbery attempts, crowd panic, fire alarms, medical emergencies, hostage scenarios, and coordinating with local law enforcement stations.
- Legal Protocols and Use of Force: Strict adherence to proportional use of force, self-defense law, post-incident evidence preservation, and reporting protocols under PSARA rules.
chunks.title: Qualification File — Armed Security Guard (NCVET Code 2022/OAFM/MEPSC/05426)
chunks.issuing_authority: Management & Entrepreneurship and Professional Skills Council (MEPSC)

chunks.chunk_text: Certified candidates are eligible for immediate empanelment with PSARA-licensed Private Security Agencies (PSAs), specialized Cash Logistics Companies, banking institutions, and critical infrastructure installations across Karnataka.
chunks.title: Qualification File — Armed Security Guard (NCVET Code 2022/OAFM/MEPSC/05426)
chunks.issuing_authority: Management & Entrepreneurship and Professional Skills Council (MEPSC)

chunks.section: Qualification Pack — Mechanic Motor Vehicle (ASDC Standards)
chunks.title: Qualification Pack — Mechanic Motor Vehicle (ASDC Standards)
chunks.issuing_authority: Directorate General of Training (DGT), MSDE / ASDC

chunks.chunk_text:
The Mechanic Motor Vehicle trade qualifies technicians to perform complete maintenance, diagnostics, servicing, and overhauling of internal combustion engines, commercial vehicles, passenger cars, and motorized two/three-wheelers.
- NSQF Level: Level 4
- Duration: 2 Years under CTS (or 400-500 hours modular QP for Automotive Service Technician).
- Entry Qualification: Passed 10th Class examination with Science and Mathematics.
- Minimum Age: 14 years (CTS) / 18 years (QP employment).
chunks.title: Qualification Pack — Mechanic Motor Vehicle (ASDC Standards)
chunks.issuing_authority: Directorate General of Training (DGT), MSDE / ASDC

chunks.chunk_text:
- Engine Systems: Disassembly, inspection, measurement, and reassembly of petrol and diesel engine components (cylinder block, piston rings, crankshaft, camshaft, valves, timing gears/belts).
- Fuel and Exhaust Systems: Servicing Common Rail Direct Injection (CRDI) diesel systems, electronic fuel injection (EFI) petrol systems, turbochargers, intercoolers, catalytic converters, and diesel particulate filters (DPF).
- Transmission and Drivetrain: Inspection and repair of manual and automatic gearboxes, clutch assemblies, propeller shafts, universal joints, differential units, and drive axles.
- Braking, Steering, and Suspension: Overhauling hydraulic, vacuum-assisted, and air brake systems; Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) diagnostics; wheel alignment and balancing; power steering racks; McPherson strut suspension.
- Auto Electrical and OBD Diagnostics: Scanning on-board vehicle electronic control units (ECUs) using OBD-II diagnostic scanners, reading fault codes (DTCs), troubleshooting starter motors, alternators, battery management, lighting, and wiring harnesses.
chunks.title: Qualification Pack — Mechanic Motor Vehicle (ASDC Standards)

chunks.section: Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) — Fitter Trade Syllabus
chunks.title: CTS Fitter Trade Syllabus and Course Qualification
chunks.issuing_authority: Directorate General of Training (DGT), MSDE

chunks.chunk_text:
The Fitter trade is a core mechanical engineering trade under CTS that develops foundational precision manufacturing, bench work, fitting, machine assembly, and maintenance competencies.
- NSQF Level: Level 4
- Duration: 2 Years (2400 hours total practical, theory, engineering drawing, and workshop calculations).
- Entry Qualification: Passed 10th class examination with Science and Mathematics.
- Certification: National Trade Certificate (NTC) awarded by NCVT upon successful All India Trade Test (AITT) assessment.
chunks.title: CTS Fitter Trade Syllabus and Course Qualification
chunks.issuing_authority: Directorate General of Training (DGT), MSDE

chunks.chunk_text:
A certified Fitter executes precision engineering tasks:
- Bench Work and Hand Tools: Precision marking, filing, sawing, chiseling, scraping, reaming, and tapping using precision hand tools within tight tolerances (up to ±0.02 mm).
- Precision Measurement: Proficient reading and handling of vernier calipers, outside/inside micrometers, vernier height gauges, dial test indicators, sine bars, and slip gauges.
- Machine Operations: Setting up and operating standard workshop machinery including sensitive drilling machines, power hacksaws, shaping machines, and pedestal grinders.
- Fasteners and Assembly: Fitting keys, splines, dowel pins, bearings, couplings, gears, pulleys, and belts onto shafts; checking alignment and concentricity.
- Pipes and Hydraulics: Basic pipe bending, threading, flanging, valve fitting; assembly and testing of pneumatic and hydraulic control circuits.
- Preventive Maintenance: Routine lubrication, bearing replacement, alignment checks, seal replacement, and troubleshooting industrial machinery.
chunks.title: CTS Fitter Trade Syllabus and Course Qualification
chunks.issuing_authority: Directorate General of Training (DGT), MSDE

chunks.chunk_text: Fitters are in high demand across public sector and private industrial units: aerospace manufacturing, defense production units (HAL, BEL), Indian Railways, machine tool plants, heavy engineering fabrication yards, and automotive assembly plants in Karnataka industrial corridors.
